pool.text: Triangle \( ABC \) (shown) has area \( 7 \). Points \( D \in BC \), \( E \in CA \), and \( F \in AB \) divide the sides cyclically in the same ratio \( \frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{CE}{EA} = \frac{AF}{FB} = 2 \). The cevians \( AD, BE, CF \) enclose an interior triangle \( \triangle PQR \). What is the exact area \( [PQR] \)?
pool.sol: By Routh's Theorem (or subtracting three corner triangles each of area \( \frac{2}{2^2 + 2 + 1}[ABC] \) via Menelaus), \[ \frac{[PQR]}{[ABC]} = \frac{(2 - 1)^2}{2^2 + 2 + 1} = \frac{1}{7}. \] Multiplying by \( [ABC] = 7 \) yields \( [PQR] = 1 \).

Multiply by \( [ABC] = 7 \) at \( k = 2 \) to get \( 1 \).
